title: A stalk is inverse image to a geometric point
statement:
If $\bar t:\Spec(\Omega)\to T$ is a geometric point, the stalk of a
sheaf (or derived object) at $\bar t$ is its inverse image along
$\bar t$.

proof.text: Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and put $P=\Spec(\Omega)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk](1), global sections $\Gamma(P,-)$ is an equivalence from abelian (or $\Lambda$-module) sheaves on $P_{\Et}$ to abelian groups (or $\Lambda$-modules); by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk](2), $\Gamma(P,\bar t^{-1}F)\cong F_{\bar t}$ naturally in $F$, with $\bar t^{-1}$ the inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $F_{\bar t}$ the stalk of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Hence, under the identification of sheaves on $P_{\Et}$ with groups, $\bar t^{-1}\cong(-)_{\bar t}$ as functors. For a derived object, represent it by a complex $F^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. The stalk functor is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so by the natural isomorphism just obtained $\bar t^{-1}$ is exact as well; both therefore act on complexes termwise, preserve quasi-isomorphisms and pass to derived categories without deriving, and the termwise natural isomorphism identifies $\bar t^{-1}F^\bullet$ with $F^\bullet_{\bar t}$, compatibly with $H^q(F^\bullet_{\bar t})\cong(\mathcal H^qF^\bullet)_{\bar t}$.
